newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE March volume up 18 pct in year, down in month.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE March volume up 18 pct in year, down in month.

text.p: The London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange said on Wednesday 16.58 million futures and options contracts traded in March, a rise of 18.3 percent from March 1996.
But the total was down from 17.45 million contracts traded in February of this year.

The exchange said the period of the three-months to March was the first time more than 50 million contracts had traded during a quarter. The first quarter 1997 total was 51.33 million contracts, a rise of 9.7 percent on the first quarter 1996.

"Continuing speculation over Italian entry to European economic and monetary union was reflected in volumes of our Eurolira futures and options contracts," said Daniel Hodson, LIFFE's chief executive.
"This sustained growth in our volumes adds further fuel to our intention to be the world centre for euro derivatives."
LIFFE's average daily volume in March was 872,429, representing an average daily nominal turnover of 187.04 billion stg ($307 billion).
During the month, FTSE 100 index futures set a daily record of 49,240 on March 20, a rise of 9.5 percent from the previous record in September 1992.
Three-month Euroswiss franc interest rate futures set a daily record of 49,137 up from the previous record of 44,673 in May 1996.
Options on three-month Eurolira futures set a monthly record of 204,752 contracts, beating the previous 188,332 record set the previous month.
